source.title: Towards Robust Temporal Activity Localization Learning with Noisy Labels
source.authors: Daizong Liu; Xiao-Ye Qu; Xiang Fang; Jian-Feng Dong; Pan Zhou; Guo-Shun Nan; Ke-Ke Tang; Wanlong Fang; Yu Cheng

record.tranche_reason: Applies noisy-label learning to temporal activity localization and reports how clean and perturbed-boundary samples behave during training.
record.gate_note: The study measures clean-versus-noisy sample losses in its TAL setting. Its cited findings from Arpit et al. and other prior work are not recorded as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: Section 3.3 and Figure 3 report the study's own direct-training loss trajectories: clean temporal-boundary labels are learned earlier than randomly perturbed boundaries. This bears on V6 in a new task, independently of the subsequent mitigation method.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that CTR improves robustness to noisy temporal-boundary annotations across three datasets. Loss separation during retraining is a supporting observation about their method.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a temporal activity localization task with perturbed moment boundaries, co-teaching, label refinement, and curriculum learning; it does not reproduce the original random-image-labeling experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports differing results across noise ratios, noise levels, datasets, and ablation settings, but these do not test the claim versions directly.

fits_no_version.finding: During CTR retraining, losses associated with most clean pairs decrease while those associated with noisy labels increase.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Co-teaching, label refinement, and curriculum learning separate clean and noisy sample losses during temporal activity localization training.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation; LREC-COLING 2024
record.problems: The results concern temporal boundary perturbations rather than random class labels. The text reports loss-distribution plots but no uncertainty estimates for these results.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were extracted: the reported benchmark tables measure localization performance under boundary-noise settings, not the training-fit, chance-test-error, or memorization outcomes named by V1–V5.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time factors relative to true labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit across corruption fractions and test error approaching chance. Localization recall under boundary perturbations does not establish these outcomes.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.

Direct identification of shared patterns learned first, completely random labels, and demonstrated eventual memorization of noisy labels. The supplied figure text provides no readable numerical endpoint establishing complete fitting.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. R1 measures learning dynamics under direct training; R2 concerns dynamics under deliberate noise mitigation and supplies no additional verdict on V6.

versions.untested_parts: Random image labels, training error, test error at chance, and unchanged architecture or hyperparameters.
Training time relative to true labels and convergence as the fraction of corrupted labels changes.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Randomly corrupted class labels, perfect training fit across corruption levels, and test error rising toward chance.
Weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, and generalization on true labels.
The study reports clean and perturbed-boundary sample losses in TAL; it does not test random labels or establish that networks learn shared real-data patterns first.

early training; exact epoch not stated

rows.measure: Per-sample loss for clean versus noisy samples.
rows.value: The text states that noisy labels take longer to learn than clean labels; Figure 3 plots their losses.
rows.note: The study describes noisy labels as harder samples and reports that their losses take longer to learn; it does not establish the broader real-patterns-before-noise claim.
rows.check: The authors explicitly report slower learning of noisy labels, consistent with V6's ordering. Coverage of only part of V6 does not make the measured effect partial. Figure 3 shows trajectories over roughly 300 epochs; the record's early-training condition describes only their initial separation. The clean-sample trajectory is the comparison baseline.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.3, Figure 3 caption and accompanying discussion, pp. 16633–16634.

rows.subject: our model
rows.operation_detail: Compared losses of clean pairs and noisy pairs with rectified soft labels during retraining.
rows.measure: Loss distributions for clean and noisy samples.
rows.value: The text says losses of most clean pairs gradually become smaller while those of most noisy labels gradually become larger.
rows.note: This concerns rectified soft labels in TAL, not random class labels or the training-error and test-error outcomes in V1–V5.
rows.check: This measures loss separation during CTR retraining with rectified labels and an explicit curriculum. It cannot establish spontaneous clean-before-noise memorization. Preserve that the losses concern rectified soft labels.

relationships.condition: Direct training of the TAL backbone on mixed clean and randomly perturbed temporal-boundary annotations, before CTR retraining.
relationships.reason: R1 reports that noisy boundaries take longer to learn than clean boundaries, supporting the clean-before-noise learning order in this setting.
relationships.display_finding: Noisy temporal boundaries took longer to learn than clean boundaries.
